prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Pasadena, Texas. The claimant was a passenger and reported knee injury. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1209; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- Witnesses and the officer say the claimant was not in the vehicle when the crash happened.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Officer narrative: Responding to a report of a rear-end collision in Pasadena, Texas, I found Driver 2's vehicle with its rear bumper pushed into the trunk area of Driver 1's vehicle. Driver 2 stated that the collision happened as described, and that account matches what the witnesses and the photographs show. Driver 1 also confirmed the sequence of events.

Passenger was reported as being in Driver 1's vehicle and complained of pain in the left knee. However, both witnesses and I observed that Passenger was not inside the vehicle when the collision occurred. It is not yet clear whether the knee injury resulted from this crash.

Some damage to Driver 1's vehicle appears to be older. A few scratches along the rear quarter panel may predate this collision, and it is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact. Driver 1 is named on the policy covering the vehicle. No citations were issued at the scene. Further follow-up is recommended to determine the extent of injuries and vehicle damage.
